correctness.rationale: The all-\(r\) proof is correct. If a spine endpoint were selected, convexity of the complement would leave at most one of its pairwise nonadjacent neighbors outside, while general position forbids two selected neighbors using the selected endpoint as a geodesic interior point; \(r\ge2\) gives a contradiction. Convexity then forces page vertices to be selected in complete pairs, and two selected page pairs violate general position along a length-three geodesic. Conversely, deleting one internal page pair leaves a convex complement because every path entering that deleted page contains the length-three spine detour and is strictly shortened by the common edge. An independent direct shortest-path enumeration for \(r=2,3,4,5,6\) found exactly \(r\) nonempty dual-general-position sets, all the internal pairs; the finite checks corroborate rather than replace the universal proof.
risks: The boundary \(r=1\) is excluded and behaves differently.

originality.rationale: The initiating dual-general-position paper explicitly treats generalized theta graphs. For \(\Theta(1,3,\ldots,3)\), its Proposition 3.6 only establishes positivity by exhibiting the two internal vertices of a length-three path; it does not give the exact maximum, classify all dual-general-position sets, or count them. value.rationale: The exact structure of dual-general-position sets refines a published generalized-theta positivity result on a standard graph family. Classifying every nonempty set and counting all maximizers for arbitrary page number is a natural structural completion, not a finite spot check.
risks: The theorem is specific to square-page books.

limitations: No claim for triangular books, longer pages, or arbitrary generalized theta graphs.
